SMTO-FIL-0046 — SMTO can't open that file link

GUID: d4f447b7-01d4-40b0-b151-a1ea6fe178d6
Slug: local-file-link-invalid
Domain: FIL · Subsystem: fil

What happened

  • The file link you selected points to a file that no longer exists, to a folder, or to a place outside the folder SMTO is allowed to open. Nothing was changed.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Ask SMTO in the conversation where the file is now, in case it was moved, renamed or deleted after the answer was written. The link still points to the old location, so it can't open a file that has moved.
  2. If the file is outside the folder SMTO's server works in, open it directly on the computer where it's stored. For safety, SMTO opens linked files only inside that one folder.
  3. If the link points to a folder, open that folder on the computer itself, or ask SMTO to list what's in it. These links can open single files only.

What success looks like

  • Selecting the link opens or downloads the file in your browser.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them, with the link text, to the person who manages SMTO. Don't ask them to widen SMTO's file access just to open one link.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The Server refused a local file link from the response because the path is empty, resolves outside the configured workspace_root, does not exist, or is not a regular file.

What this means

  • A local UI file link is empty, resolves outside the workspace root, does not exist or is not a file. Why this can happen

  • A local UI file link is empty, resolves outside the workspace root, does not exist or is not a file.

How to diagnose it

  • Check the resolved path and workspace root; the UI's local-file boundary is separate from remote Gateway paths.

How to fix it

  • Compare the linked path with the Server's workspace_root setting (defaults to the directory the Server started in); relative paths resolve against it. Regenerate or correct the link to an existing regular file under that root, and do not relax the workspace containment check.
  • Choose an existing file within the intended workspace through the supported file flow. Do not bypass path containment or broaden policy merely to open an untrusted link.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • An existing intended file resolves within the workspace and opens through the supported route.

What not to do

  • Do not silently substitute a different target for a saved run or move its existing execution authority.
